questions.question_text: What is the primary structure of a single cycle in thePomodoroTechnique?

options.text: 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break
25 minutes of work followed by a 5-minute break
30 minutes of work followed by a 15-minute break
20 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute breakCorrect Answer: B) 25 minutes of work followed by a 5-minute break

questions.question_text: What is one key benefit of thePomodoroTechnique for students?

options.text: It eliminates the need for planning study sessions
It increases focus by working in short, manageable intervals
It encourages multitasking during study time
It allows students to study for hours without breaksCorrect Answer: B) It increases focus by working in short, manageable intervals

questions.question_text: When applying thePomodoroTechnique to study sessions, what is a recommended strategy for maximizing focus?

options.text: Work on multiple subjects during a single Pomodoro
Check social media briefly to stay motivated
Focus on only one task or topic per Pomodoro
Stop working if the task isn’t completed in 25 minutesCorrect Answer: C) Focus on only one task or topic per Pomodoro

questions.question_text: How can thePomodoroTechnique be adapted for a student who finds 25-minute intervals too short for complex tasks?

options.text: Skip breaks entirely to maintain momentum
Extend work intervals to 30 or 50 minutes with proportional breaks
Reduce work intervals to 15 minutes for easier focus
Ignore the timer and work until the task is completeCorrect Answer: B) Extend work intervals to 30 or 50 minutes with proportional breaks

questions.question_text: What is a recommended activity during a short 5-minute break to prevent burnout?

options.text: Review notes from the previous Pomodoro to reinforce learning
Scroll through social media to relax quickly
Stand up and stretch to improve blood flow
Start planning the next study task immediatelyCorrect Answer: C) Stand up and stretch to improve blood flow

questions.question_text: Why are breaks an essential part of thePomodoroTechnique in preventing burnout?

options.text: They allow students to complete more tasks in less time
They provide a cognitive reset and reduce mental fatigue
They encourage students to take longer naps during the day
They help students avoid studying altogetherCorrect Answer: B) They provide a cognitive reset and reduce mental fatigue
